ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

recipes.name: Olive Oil Ice Cream, circulator
recipes.description: Scaled 0.8× from the 1 kg formula. All ratios unchanged — PAC, POD, fat, MSNF and total solids are identical to the full batch. Sized to two 16 oz Ball jars in a circulator bath.

payload.sheetDescription: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

recipes.name: Olive Oil Ice Cream, circulator
recipes.description: Scaled 0.8× from the 1 kg formula. All ratios unchanged — PAC, POD, fat, MSNF and total solids are identical to the full batch. Sized to two 16 oz Ball jars in a circulator bath.

payload.sheetDescription: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

fields: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.
Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

recipes.name: Olive Oil Ice Cream, circulator
recipes.description: Scaled 0.8× from the 1 kg formula. All ratios unchanged — PAC, POD, fat, MSNF and total solids are identical to the full batch. Sized to two 16 oz Ball jars in a circulator bath.

fields: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.
Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

versions.sheetDescription: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

recipes.name: Olive Oil Ice Cream, circulator
recipes.description: Scaled 0.8× from the 1 kg formula. All ratios unchanged — PAC, POD, fat, MSNF and total solids are identical to the full batch. Sized to two 16 oz Ball jars in a circulator bath.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

versions.sheetDescription: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

recipes.name: Olive Oil Ice Cream, circulator
recipes.description: Scaled 0.8× from the 1 kg formula. All ratios unchanged — PAC, POD, fat, MSNF and total solids are identical to the full batch. Sized to two 16 oz Ball jars in a circulator bath.

ingredient.name: Heavy cream, 36% fat

source.fat: panel reconciled three ways against a 36% regulatory floor

ingredient.note: Panel implied 40%, 37% and 37% by three routes. Carton says "36% minimum", which is a floor, not a value. Contains gellan gum at an unpublished level — roughly 0.03–0.09 g at this cream weight, an estimate with no published spec.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

versions.sheetDescription: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

ingredient.note: Carton states 3.5%. A previous carton computed to 3.28% from the panel — worth re-reading each time.

ingredient.name: Heavy cream, 36% fat

source.fat: panel reconciled three ways against a 36% regulatory floor

ingredient.note: Panel implied 40%, 37% and 37% by three routes. Carton says "36% minimum", which is a floor, not a value. Contains gellan gum at an unpublished level — roughly 0.03–0.09 g at this cream weight, an estimate with no published spec.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.

versions.sheetDescription: Silky and quietly savoury. Fresh olive oil adds a gentle fruitiness without overwhelming the cream, and a little more salt than you would think carries it. Serve it soft, with flaky salt.

ingredient.name: Graza Drizzle extra virgin olive oil
ingredient.note: Liquid at serving temperature, so it cannot join the fat crystal network that stabilises air cells.

ingredient.name: Skim milk powder
ingredient.note: Heat class is never printed on US retail packaging and materially affects flavour.

ingredient.name: Allulose
ingredient.note: The least certain constant in this formula. Browns with milk proteins, so it goes in after the heat step.

ingredient.name: Dextrose
ingredient.note: PAC moved from 1.9 to 1.66 between generations of the predecessor app, and nothing on any page recorded that it had.

method.instruction: Whisk 1.2 g soy lecithin into the 40 g of Drizzle. Cover, leave at room temperature.
method.purpose: It's lipophilic — it disperses poorly if added to the water phase.

method.leadIn: Gum slurry — the only high-heat step
method.instruction: Toss 1.68 g of the gum blend with the sucrose. Whisk into the milk in a small saucepan. Heat, whisking constantly, then pull off.
method.aside: At 120 g this is a thin layer in the pan. It scorches and evaporates faster than a larger volume would — keep whisking and don’t walk away.

method.instruction: Whisk the remaining sucrose, plus 22.4 g SMP, 12 g dextrose and 3.2 g salt, into the remaining milk and all 252.8 g of cream. Add the hot gum slurry. Immersion blend.
Tare, pour, check.
method.purpose: Mismatched jars hit core temperature at different times and you would be timing off the wrong one.
method.aside: Two-piece lids finger-tight only — the headspace air expands and needs to vent rather than build pressure.

method.instruction: Start the clock when the jar core reaches temperature.
method.purpose: With 379 g in a squat wide-mouth jar the come-up is much faster than a single large vessel.
method.aside: Probe the core rather than trusting the estimate. Invert each jar once or twice partway through.

method.instruction: Combine both jars, stir in the 20 g allulose off the heat until dissolved, then straight into an ice bath.
method.aside: Allulose skips the hold — it browns readily with milk proteins.

method.instruction: Hold covered in the fridge.
Mix still at 4 °C. Pour the lecithin-oil blend in a thin stream under a running immersion blender.
method.aside: Never heat this oil.

method.instruction: Freeze immediately.
Harden, then temper before serving.

beforeYouStart.text: Taste the Graza straight. Polyphenols degrade with light and oxygen, and the squeeze bottle offers less protection than dark glass. An old bottle at 40 g will disappear entirely.
Check the cream’s actual butterfat. The carton states a 36% minimum, which is a floor.
